transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-09
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Martin (Redwood AE); Priya Shah (Redwood SE); Sara Kim (Ridgeview CISO); Tom Delgado (Lead Architect); Meera Patel (Compliance)
---
Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): discuss data residency, HIPAA scope, logging retention, dedicated/private options and next steps
---
00:00 Alex Martin: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um I'm Alex Martin, account exec for Redwood, and with me is Priya our solutions engineer.
00:07 Sara Kim: hi Alex, thanks. Quick note, we'll mostly focus on compliance/residency concerns for our LLM usage across customer segments.
00:13 Priya Shah: great, can you give us a top-level sense of the workloads you're planning? is this customer chat bots, document processing?
00:20 Tom Delgado: mostly document ingestion, statement summarization, a little chat for customer service. Some customers in the EU, and a handful of health-related partners where HIPAA may apply.
00:30 Meera Patel: and from compliance, we need strict controls on logs, ideally no raw PII in logs, retention limits, audit trails, and evidence for auditors.
00:38 Alex Martin: understood. Quick overview from our side — Redwood offers Hosted API (fast to start), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools with VPC peering and network controls), and Private (customer-managed control plane / on-prem). Each has different tradeoffs for residency and logging.
00:52 Priya Shah: to add, Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and we can place capacity in region X vs region Y; Private lets you keep control of all data paths and keys. Hosted by default stores metadata in region where the account is provisioned, but we do have EU-hosted options — though there are caveats for logs and telemetry.
01:10 Sara Kim: caveats like what?
01:12 Priya Shah: on Hosted we retain some telemetry for observability and billing; for regulated data, we recommend Dedicated or Private so we can restrict or disable certain logs, and integrate with your KMS. Our Hosted offering can be configured with reduced telemetry but not full on-prem isolation.
01:28 Meera Patel: for HIPAA, we need BAAs and assurance that ePHI won't leave our control — how does Dedicated vs Private compare?
01:36 Alex Martin: good question. We can sign a BAA for Dedicated and Private. Dedicated is customer-isolated from noisy tenants and supports VPC peering + customer-managed KMS in many cases. Private (on-prem) gives you the tightest control — full control plane in your environment.
01:49 Tom Delgado: does Dedicated let us put model weights and KV cache in EU-only hardware? we need processing for EU customers to stay in EU for GDPR.
01:56 Priya Shah: yes, we can provision Dedicated capacity in specific regions; model weights and inference compute will run in the region you choose. For strict GDPR residency, Private or Dedicated in the EU region is recommended. Hosted EU region is possible but telemetry/backup patterns need to be reviewed.
02:10 Alex Martin: and for audit logs, we can push audit logs to your S3/GCS bucket or SIEM via secure transfer for Dedicated and Private. Hosted can export logs but there are limits and retention policies that are fixed on the hosted tier.
02:24 Meera Patel: when you say logs, what exactly is captured? full prompts, token-level traces, response text? we cannot keep raw customer input in logs for certain classes.
02:34 Priya Shah: good point — typical logs include request metadata, timestamps, status codes, and optionally prompts and responses for debugging. We support masking and redaction rules, and we can disable storing request/response bodies for Dedicated/Private. For Hosted, you can opt out of request/response retention but we still keep billing-level telemetry.
02:54 Tom Delgado: can we get an example mask policy? like remove account numbers, SSNs before logs persist.
02:59 Priya Shah: yes, we have built-in PII redaction patterns and you can provide custom regex-based filters. For Dedicated/Private we can implement pre-ingest masking, or we can apply post-processing before logs are stored.
03:12 Sara Kim: encryption key control — do you support bringing your own key (BYOK) / HSM?
03:17 Alex Martin: yes, for Dedicated and Private we support BYOK via KMS integrations and HSM-backed keys in some deployments. Hosted supports our managed KMS, and we have a path to BYOK for enterprise hosted contracts but that's typically on a case-by-case basis.
03:34 Meera Patel: auditors want proof of separation of duties and RBAC. how granular is the RBAC? can we restrict developer access to production models and logs?
03:42 Priya Shah: our RBAC supports role-based permissions at route/model level and you can restrict access to logs and model deployments. For Dedicated/Private you control the mapping to your identity provider (SAML/SSO). For Hosted we support SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning.
03:57 Tom Delgado: network connectivity — we use Azure ExpressRoute and AWS Direct Connect in different markets. Can Dedicated peer into our VPC and avoid public internet?
04:05 Priya Shah: yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering and private connectivity, including peering via Direct Connect/ExpressRoute. For Private on-prem, of course, you keep traffic internal. Hosted would traverse public endpoints unless you use private endpoints in some cloud regions — we can discuss specifics.
04:21 Sara Kim: what about PCI for card data in chat flows? we cannot log full card PANs and need tokenization.
04:28 Alex Martin: we recommend tokenization at the customer's edge — strip or tokenize PANs before sending to Redwood. We can also configure request filtering to drop or redact fields. For PCI scope reduction we advise never persisting card data and use masking.
04:41 Meera Patel: GDPR — how do you handle data subject access requests (DSARs) and right to be forgotten?
04:46 Priya Shah: for Dedicated/Private you control data retention and can delete logs on request. Hosted requires a process where we can purge account-level data but there may be backups with retention windows; we will outline the DSAR flow in the security docs.
04:58 Tom Delgado: what's the SLA for Dedicated latency and availability? we need consistent 99th percentile latency under 200ms for token generation for certain routes.
05:06 Alex Martin: we have SLA-backed latency targets for Dedicated at certain commits; exact numbers depend on instance sizing and batching configuration. Priya can follow up with benchmark results matching your expected request profile.
05:18 Priya Shah: if you can share your QPS and typical sequence lengths we can run sample benchmark on our Dedicated pool to validate 99th percentile. That's usually part of the pilot.
05:28 Sara Kim: are there existing customers in financial services using Dedicated with PCI/HIPAA?
05:32 Alex Martin: yes, we have a handful of banks and fintechs — some of the references are on the security doc. we'll share anonymized case studies.
05:40 Tom Delgado: curious on telemetry — do you retain gradients, model updates, or anything that could leak training signals?
05:45 Priya Shah: we don't persist gradients from inference. For fine-tuning workflows, that's separate and usually done in a controlled training environment. Inference telemetry is limited to what we've described; we can disable payload retention in Dedicated/Private.
06:00 Meera Patel: for logs forwarded to our SIEM, we need log signing and tamper-evidence for audit. supported?
06:06 Priya Shah: we can sign logs and provide immutable append-only logs when integrated with customer-side S3 + Glacier or SIEM; for Private you can enforce immutability policies. We'll include options in the diagram.
06:18 Alex Martin: another practical question — timeline and procurement. do you have an internal timeline for decision?
06:23 Sara Kim: timeline is tight; we'd like pilot running by mid-August and production by Q4 if things look good. procurement will need security review and a BAA addendum.
06:33 Tom Delgado: budget is TBD but we're aiming for a Dedicated pilot first to validate performance and residency.
06:38 Meera Patel: legal will want contract language around data residency guarantees and breach notification windows.
06:44 Alex Martin: understood. We'll include proposed contractual language in the materials.
06:48 Priya Shah: quick technical note — for GDPR residency we recommend Dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 for EU customers and configuring routing policies so EU traffic stays in EU. For cross-border requests, we can implement policy-based routing and fallbacks.
07:05 Tom Delgado: do you do model variant fallbacks? like serve a smaller model if larger model doesn't exist in region?
07:10 Priya Shah: yes, our smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants; we can set policy to avoid cross-region fallbacks if strict residency is required.
07:21 Sara Kim: regarding telemetry again — can we redact or never collect prompts that match certain regex patterns? e.g., national IDs or SSNs.
07:29 Priya Shah: yes, custom regex redaction on the ingest path is supported for Dedicated/Private. We can run a short script to show how redaction works in practice.
07:40 Tom Delgado: what's the cost delta roughly between Hosted and Dedicated? we expect Dedicated to be more expensive but predictable.
07:47 Alex Martin: yes Dedicated has a fixed monthly commitment for reserved capacity; it can be more cost-effective at scale. We'll send pricing bands after we size the pilot.
07:56 Meera Patel: for compliance, we need evidence of SOC 2 Type II and penetration test reports. do you have these?
08:02 Alex Martin: yes we have SOC 2 Type II reports, pen test summaries, and a security whitepaper. We'll attach those.
08:09 Tom Delgado: slightly off-topic — what about model fine-tuning or storing proprietary models? we may want to bring our models later.
08:15 Priya Shah: Private supports customer-hosted models; Dedicated can host customer model artifacts in your region with appropriate access controls. Hosted has options but often not recommended for IP-sensitive models.
08:26 Sara Kim: suggestion from compliance — we want the pilot to include sample DSAR and log purge flows so auditors can validate.
08:33 Alex Martin: agreed, we can build that into the pilot acceptance criteria.
08:38 Priya Shah: for the technical deep dive we'll demo Dedicated network flow, key management, log redaction, and run a small throughput test tailored to your sequences.
08:47 Meera Patel: any limitations around backups and cold storage? we need to ensure backups are also region-locked.
08:53 Priya Shah: Dedicated/Private backups can be configured to stay in-region; Hosted backups may have global replication by default — we will detail that in the docs.
09:04 Tom Delgado: okay, next steps recap?
09:07 Alex Martin: I'll send the SOC2/HIPAA/PCI docs, and a short security FAQ. Priya will share Dedicated network diagram and proposed pilot runbook and we'll schedule the technical deep dive for week of 2026-07-20. Tom will send sample logs and retention policy.
09:24 Meera Patel: thanks, when you send the docs please highlight the parts relevant to DSAR and log masking.
09:29 Alex Martin: noted. Any final questions?
09:32 Sara Kim: none from me. thanks everyone.
09:34 Tom Delgado: good session, thanks.
09:36 Alex Martin: thanks all — we'll follow up with the materials and a calendar invite for the technical call.
